newsitem.title: BULGARIA: SIZE OF BULGARIA TELECOM SALE NEGOTIABLE - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: SIZE OF BULGARIA TELECOM SALE NEGOTIABLE - MINISTER.

text.p: Bulgaria may sell a larger stake than the planned 25 percent in the Bulgarian Telecommunications Company (BTC), depending on negotiations with potential buyers, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov said on Monday.
Bozhkov told reporters after a cabinet meeting the government would not fix for the time being the size of the stake to be sold.
"It will be decided during the negotiations and the choosing of the buyer," he said.
World Bank official Kenneth Lay, who visited Sofia at the weekend, urged the government to consider selling whatever share in the BTC would bring the best price.
Bozhkov said Bulgaria would seek an operator as a buyer in a bid to guarantee its national interests but not a firm which would play the role of a broker selling on the BTC stake later.

"The most important thing is how to guarantee the national interest, but this does not depened on the size of the stake as guarantees can be lodged in the venture's rules. In this respect Germany's and France's model will be followed," he said, referring to other big European telecoms privatisations.

Bulgaria suffers the lowest foreign investment levels in the region and relies solely on external lending for around $1 billion of debt payments due this year, a third of which is in the first quarter.

Preliminary figures show that BTC's pre-tax profit last year was three times higher than in 1995, when the company's pre-tax profit was 2.7 million levs against 3.1 million in 1994, BTC spokeswoman Vera Pavlova told Reuters.
BTC revenue in 1996 was 2.4 times higher than in 1995, when the company's revenue was 17 million levs against 12.6 million in 1994, she said.
She was unable to give figures for 1996.
